planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown starts in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun.

directions: Plant in well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun; Glitter tolerates more light than many silver-leafed heucheras and develops its best shine with at least a few hours of direct sun. This Terra Nova Nurseries introduction forms a dense, neat mound of mirror-bright silver leaves patterned with contrasting black veins and a violet-toned reverse, marketed as a glossier improvement on the older cultivar 'Silver Scrolls'. Large sprays of fuchsia-pink flowers bloom from early summer into fall on wiry stems above the foliage. Its fast growth and tidy habit suit edging, rock gardens, and containers as well as mixed shade borders.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade.

directions: Plant divisions in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade. Pink Stardust forms an evergreen clump of silvery, mint-green foliage topped from spring through summer by unusually large, star-shaped pink-and-white flowers on sturdy stems held well above the leaves. As a sterile, rust-free heucherella it never sets seed and, unlike many heuchera, its crown does not heave out of the soil over time, so it does not need periodic lifting and replanting. It is reported to hold up well even in Deep South gardens, tolerating more heat and humidity than many shade perennials.

directions: Plant divisions in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade. Viking Ship carries maple-shaped leaves that emerge silvered in spring and develop patches of green, lime, and red, with some leaves showing partially detached leaflets for an unusually ragged, textured look. Tall spires of coral-pink, star-shaped flowers rise well above the foliage from late spring into summer. Like other heucherella, it forms a mounding, evergreen clump that does not need the periodic crown-lifting that many heuchera eventually require.

directions: Plant divisions in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade. Majestic Mist forms a clumping mound of bright green leaves heavily speckled with white and marked with prominent red veins year-round, taking on additional pink tones in fall; it is described as a more stable, more strongly variegated counterpart to the older cultivar 'Mystic Mist'. Foamy white flower spikes rise above the foliage in spring. Unlike many groundcover-type tiarella, it spreads by clumping rather than by stolons, so it stays tidier and is easier to keep within bounds in a mixed shade border.

directions: Plant divisions in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade. Starfish is named for its deeply cut, star-shaped leaves in green marked with black, which take on strong bronze tones through winter for season-long foliage interest. Cream flowers opening from pink buds appear in spring and are known to rebloom later in the season more reliably than many tiarella cultivars. It forms a tidy, compact clump rather than spreading aggressively, making it well suited to woodland gardens and shaded borders where a well-behaved foamflower is needed.
